title: Choose Dataflow Gen2, Copy, or Code
purpose: Choose the transformation surface, then expose Dataflow Gen2 staging internals and its main operational trap.
accessibleSummary: A branching decision asks whether work is low-code shaping, primarily data movement, or code-intensive engineering. The branches select Dataflow Gen2, Pipeline Copy, or Notebook and SQL tools. The Dataflow path shows managed staging and destination writes, with a warning not to depend on internal staging items.
longDescription: Start with the dominant responsibility. Low-code Power Query shaping selects Dataflow Gen2. Movement with minimal shaping selects Copy activity or Copy job. Complex algorithms, streaming, reusable software engineering, or engine-native SQL select notebook or SQL-model tooling. The Dataflow branch flows through managed staging to configured destinations. Internal DataflowsStaging items are implementation details, not user-managed contracts.

nodes.label: What is the dominant need?
nodes.summary: Choose by transformation complexity and ownership rather than by connector availability alone.
nodes.detail: Choose by transformation complexity and ownership rather than by connector availability alone. Classify the work as low-code shaping, movement, or code-intensive transformation.
nodes.whyItMatters: A defensible tool-selection branch depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

inputs: Source, target, transformation specification, and team skills
processing: Classify the work as low-code shaping, movement, or code-intensive transformation
drill.example: A team separates simple cleansing from a custom graph algorithm before selecting tools.
controls: Transformation complexity, scale, CI/CD, and operations
failureModes: Selecting one tool for every stage creates brittle workarounds

nodes.label: Dataflow Gen2
nodes.summary: Use Power Query for visual, low-code shaping with configured destinations.
nodes.detail: Use Power Query for visual, low-code shaping with configured destinations. Apply joins, cleansing, typing, and aggregation.
nodes.whyItMatters: Curated rows for one or more destinations depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Microsoft positions Dataflow Gen2 for low-code shaping before load.

inputs: Connected data and Power Query steps
processing: Apply joins, cleansing, typing, and aggregation
outputs: Curated rows for one or more destinations
drill.example: A business analyst standardizes customer extracts and loads a lakehouse table.
failureModes: A non-folding transformation moves excessive data into mashup compute

nodes.label: Pipeline Copy
nodes.summary: Use Copy for orchestrated movement with limited transformation.
nodes.detail: Use Copy for orchestrated movement with limited transformation. Move data with pipeline scheduling, dependency, and retry controls.
nodes.whyItMatters: Copied data at the destination depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Pipelines and copy options are the movement and orchestration surfaces.

inputs: Source and sink connections plus mapping
processing: Move data with pipeline scheduling, dependency, and retry controls
drill.example: A pipeline bulk-copies raw ERP tables before Spark transformation.
failureModes: Embedding complex business shaping in copy mappings becomes unmaintainable

nodes.label: Notebook or SQL model
nodes.summary: Use code or SQL-declarative tools for complex, testable, engine-native transformation.
nodes.detail: Use code or SQL-declarative tools for complex, testable, engine-native transformation. Execute code-first or declarative transformations on the target engine.
nodes.whyItMatters: Versioned engineered tables depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

inputs: Complex algorithms, streaming, SQL models, tests, and source control
processing: Execute code-first or declarative transformations on the target engine
drill.example: A Spark notebook parses nested telemetry while dbt models stable warehouse SQL.
failureModes: Procedural code hides dependencies unless explicitly modeled

nodes.label: Managed Gen2 staging
nodes.summary: Dataflow Gen2 may use internal lakehouse and warehouse staging for SQL scale-out.
nodes.detail: Dataflow Gen2 may use internal lakehouse and warehouse staging for SQL scale-out. Stage and execute intermediates on managed SQL compute.
nodes.whyItMatters: Prepared rows ready for destination write depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Gen2 provisions internal staging lakehouse and warehouse items for SQL-backed processing.

inputs: Published Dataflow plan and intermediate rows
processing: Stage and execute intermediates on managed SQL compute
outputs: Prepared rows ready for destination write
drill.example: A large join stages intermediate data before loading a warehouse.
failureModes: Treating system staging objects as stable user-facing tables

nodes.label: Do not own staging internals
nodes.summary: Depending on or editing DataflowsStaging items creates an unsupported operational coupling.
nodes.detail: Depending on or editing DataflowsStaging items creates an unsupported operational coupling. Avoid direct reads, writes, permissions changes, or downstream dependencies.
nodes.whyItMatters: A dataflow whose managed internals remain replaceable depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

inputs: System-named staging items visible in a workspace
processing: Avoid direct reads, writes, permissions changes, or downstream dependencies
outputs: A dataflow whose managed internals remain replaceable
drill.example: Consumers read the configured destination, never DataflowsStagingWarehouse.
failureModes: A report built on staging breaks when Fabric recreates implementation state
